en: "Ufufufuuu!{w}I dunno what you're talking about~"{w}
note: Child voice (hiragana source). Closing ~ stands for the source's note mark. Editorial: hiragana ufufu = "Ufufu" (review_notes convention; Hee hee is Gurtia's katakana laugh); long vowel kept as uuu.

en: "UWOOOOOmmm...!!"{w}
note: Creature's English kept as written (glossary note); full-width letters converted to ASCII.

en: "So. That. Means...{w}one more tiiime!"{w}
note: da-ka-ra is spelled out syllable by syllable for emphasis; rendered as clipped words.

en: "Fwooooo!{w}Don't NYOP ME!!"{w}
"Heeere goes... KA..."{w}
note: Her catchphrase (4884 in slice 067, 'sore, dokkaan!!') cut off mid-word. Accuracy: aligned to 4884's existing English "Heeere goes... KABOOM!!" (cut after KA) instead of asking for 4884 to change. Editorial: one source ellipsis = "..." (brief); cut-off stays after KA, matching 4884.

en: "HEEEEELP!?{w}IYAAAAAAANPOS!!"{w}
note: Kept as written: the Japanese scream 'iyaan' fused with NYOPS.

en: "Hm?{w}Huh? Huuuh?"{w}{p}"Hey, Nyoppu.{w}There's somebody here I've never seen before!"{w}
note: Nyoppu = her pet name for the creature (romanized). 'mikakenai ko' (an unfamiliar kid) = the party; kept number-neutral as 'somebody'.

en: "PU?{w}OH! UNKNOWN NYOS."{w}{p}"HALLO.{w}SAY SAY SAY TO ME!!{w}NYOP or PRIN?"{w}{p}"...BINGO! PRINGO!!{w}NYOP! Me too.{w}HAHAHAHAHA!!"{w}
note: Kept as written, full-width converted to ASCII. The party's answer happens off-text between pages.

en: At its request, you shook hands with the strange creature.{w}
"Now you're friends.{w}Booooring."{w}{p}"...Nyoppu, that one there says{w}you're gro-oss{w}and stiiinky."{w}
note: kimoi = gross/creepy, kusai = smelly; drawn-out tattling tone kept. 'sono ko' (that kid) = the party member/party, kept neutral as 'that one there'. She is lying to provoke it (they just shook hands).

en: "W...Whoooooooy!?{w}Why feeling Nyopness!{w}I'm very saddrin!!"{w}
Memories lead gently to death, and oblivion lights the way to tomorrow.{w}None can know which is the happier.{w}My heart is shut away, twofold, threefold.{w}
note: Inscription/monologue in literary register, as the source. Accuracy: 'shi ni itari' read as memories leading (one) to death, in parallel with oblivion lighting tomorrow; 'memories go to their death' made memories and oblivion the same thing and broke the 'which is happier' contrast.

en: You have already defeated the one who was here.{w}
There is a mysterious altar, shining white.{w}
As you approached, a mysterious light appeared.{w}It shone fiercely, as if in warning.{w}
note: fushigi na hikari kept lowercase 'mysterious light' (not in glossary; may be the boss's display name in the monster data).

en:
The mysterious light swelled and shrank over and over,
until at last it took a single form.{w}{p}You found yourselves facing a figure that blazed with proud brilliance, utterly out of place in the depths of the earth.{w}
You routed the mysterious light.{w}
note: Same pattern as earlier 'You routed X.' rows.

en: There is a mysterious altar, shining white.{w}{p}Many lights drift above the altar.{w}They look like the remains of the mysterious light you routed.{w}
What appeared was a great shadow.{w}A memory of the distant Age of Creation, kept by the land itself.{w}The forms of the gods as they once were now return to life.{w}
note: 'great shadow' matches slice 000 (SCDWMAP:14). Not the Divine Shadow (shinei) term. Editorial: "memory ... remembered" was redundant; kept = stored in the land's memory.

en:
The great shadow fades away.
Nothing has been left behind.{w}
note: Mirrors slice 000 SCDWMAP:14 ('Something has been left behind'), here with nothing.
